basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 6.' and it opens '(Vers. 6.) Filii Cham, Chus, et Mesraim, et Phuth, et Chanaan. Chus usque hodie ab'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 6.) Filii Cham, Chus, et Mesraim, et Phuth, et Chanaan. Chus usque hodie ab Hebraeis Aethiopia nuncupatur: Mesraim, Aegyptus: Phuth, Libyes. A quo et Mauritaniae fluvius usque in praesens Phuth dicitur, omnisque circa eum regio Phutensis. Multi scriptores tam Graeci quam Latini, hujus rei testes sunt. Quare autem in una tantum climatis parte, antiquum Libyae nomen resederit, et reliqua terra vocata sit Africa, disserere non hujus loci nec temporis est. Porro Chanaan obtinuit terram, quam Judaei deinceps possederunt, ejectis Chananaeis.
